evidence.text: The schema-quarantine queue grew rapidly after producer release 4.0 began emitting a new `taxRegion` field as a nested object instead of a string.
The consumer contract still required `taxRegion` to be a string; quarantined messages failed that exact validation rule.
Messages from producers still on release 3.9 passed validation and were processed normally.
The quarantine service does not alter message payloads; it stores the original bytes plus validation metadata.
A replay that bypassed validation allowed malformed 4.0 messages into billing, where 17% were assigned the default tax region and produced incorrect tax calculations.

A compatibility adapter converting the new object to the legacy string representation allowed 40 sampled messages to pass validation; five spot-checked bills used the expected tax region, but no full financial reconciliation was run.

During a ten-minute window after quarantine-worker capacity increased by 25%, queue-age growth slowed while the producer-4.0 validation-failure fraction was unchanged; incoming malformed-message volume also fell 9% during the window.
Muting the quarantine alert changed pager volume only; validation failures and queue growth continued.
Storage checksums for quarantined payloads matched producer-side checksums.

Release 4.0 code diff and artifact metadata show that taxRegion serialization changed from a string to a nested object while the shared contract version metadata remained unchanged; the producer team confirmed both observations.
After producer 4.0 was rolled back, new validation failures returned to baseline while the existing quarantine backlog drained.
A separate alert indicated elevated disk latency on one quarantine node, but failures occurred across nodes with normal disk latency as well.
Release records show producer 4.0 was promoted despite unchanged shared-contract version metadata; incident artifacts do not record why the release process permitted that mismatch.

In a prior staging drill, quarantine paging was the only automated signal of schema-validation failures; when paging was disabled, the failing queue grew for 18 minutes until an operator manually opened the dashboard.

hypotheses.text: The quarantine validator created the malformed `taxRegion` payloads.
Producer schema drift caused the validation failures.
Quarantine backlog contributed to customer-visible processing delay after malformed messages were rejected.
Storage corruption in the quarantine tier materially altered the rejected payloads.
The release process permitted producer 4.0 to ship without a required contract-version update.

edges.from: release process permitting unchanged contract version

actions.text: Roll producer 4.0 back or deploy the compatibility adapter.
Increase quarantine worker capacity during the incident.
Disable schema validation so producer-4.0 messages proceed directly to billing.
Disable quarantine paging for the duration of the incident.
Drop quarantined messages to reduce queue age.
